item: BnF fr.20140 f.35r-36r, Charles de Danzay to the Cardinal of Lorraine, Copenhagen, 27 Jan 1557 (f.36r first classified on its own at N3, then ruled part of the same letter)
final_class: N4 (no prior decipherment located; key `published`, Tomokiyo 2026; depth D2, about 77%)
near_miss: Several public items would trip a naive 'is anything public?' gate. (1) Tomokiyo's cryptiana danzay.htm (22 Feb 2026) prints the reconstructed 1557 key table and lists f.35 by folio, but marks it 'not deciphered' and prints no plaintext. A gate keyed on 'key published' or 'folio named on a cipher site' would wrongly block it. (2) Bourdeau's repo napoleon/unsolved.txt has a 'Danzay to Henry III (1574) Solved' line, and Ryabov 2025 (Quaestio Rossica 13/4) prints full decipherments and a key for Danzay's letters of 14 Oct 1574 and 28 Feb 1578. That is a different cipher and a different volume, so a sender-name match plus 'solved' would be a false block. (3) Delavaud 1911, p.74 n.3, cites 'fr.20140 (fos 16-56)', the very folio range, but only as a finding-aid list, and he calls the letters 'dépêches inédites'. (4) Cuisiat 1998 no. 486 (June 1558) has the Cardinal acknowledging 'les lettres du sr. de Danzay', which is receipt, not print. (5) Daussy 2001/2004/2015 and Teulet name Danzay but carry no 1557 letter. Process near-misses, which cost audit time but not the item: Tomokiyo's 'vol. ix' mis-citation of Handlingar XI sent check-solved to the wrong volume. Daussy 2001 was mislabelled as a Danzay study, which cost a borrow attempt and ASKS row 26; its chapter title shows it is about Duplessis-Mornay.

item: WVO 126, Orange to Elector August, Brussels 16 Sept 1564, cipher postscript (Dresden HStA Locat 8510/5 f.139)
final_class: N4 (no prior decipherment located; key `period`, from siblings WVO 98 f.67 and 124 f.135; depth D3, about 98%; KHA Collectie Japikse witness named)
near_miss: Several public items would trip a naive gate. (1) The WVO record lists a KHA minute (A11-XIVi-04-26) 'met een Zeitung' that may hold the postscript in clear. It is unimaged and unseen, and would make the item N0 in substance if it matches. The original check-solved said 'manuscript only' and missed this witness row. (2) Sibling letters 98, 74 and 153 carry 'met de oplossing' in WVO, and 124's contemporary decipherment sits in the same Dresden file. These are period decipherments of the same system (System B) but of other letters. (3) Groen, Archives t.I, Lettre LXXXII prints Orange to August of April 1564 (124's clear letter), so a sender-recipient-year gate would trip on it. (4) The event itself, Elisabeth of Valois's illness and miscarriage in August 1564, is printed in Cabié 1903 pp.289-290 (Saint-Sulpice). (5) Rachfahl II.1 cites 'Dresd. Arch. Locat 8510' often. (6) Four small letters 'e e r e' above line 1 look like a gloss but contradict the key. (7) A WVO editor (Huysman, 26 Sept 2026) named the KHA Collectie Japikse copies as the likeliest place for an earlier decipherment. They are unpublished and unseen.

item: WVO 53, Orange to Elector August, Breda 24 Oct 1561, cipher postscript (Dresden Loc. 9941/3 f.266r-v)
final_class: N4 (no prior decipherment located, for a cryptanalytic reading; key `ours`; depth D3, S 356 M 8 of 364)
near_miss: Several public items would trip a naive gate. (1) Japikse, Correspondentie van Willem den Eerste I (1934), prints the Prince's cipher passages deciphered in spaced type, and the KHA holds a Japikse copy of 53. A 'sender's edition prints decipherments' gate would trip, but the edition ends in September 1561 (index pp.386-389). The copy is unpublished preparatory work, and the WVO editor names it as the likeliest place for a prior decipherment. (2) The gist is printed from other senders. The Don Carlos and Juana marriage rumour is in Gachard, Don Carlos et Philippe II, and the Vendôme/Navarre claim is common in print, so a gist search hits the event, not the letter. (3) The phrase 'dem printzen zu hispanien' returns 300 Google Books hits (RTA 1555, Groen), all other letters. Process near-miss: p2 (f.266v) was never fetched at first, so the first reading covered half the postscript. Rule: count PDF pages before cropping.

item: WVO 57, Elector August to Orange, Torgau 18 Nov 1561, cipher enclosure on p3 (KHA A 11/XIV B/41-6)
final_class: N4 (no prior decipherment located; key `period`, System A from the contemporary decipherment of sibling WVO 74; depth D3, about 98%)
near_miss: This is the strongest naive-gate trap of the batch. The very letter is calendared in print: Demandt, 'Nassau-oranische Korrespondenzen' I, HessJb 38 (1988) p.78 nr. 113, cited in WVO as 'DNOK', with nr. 115 for the 23 Nov postscript. A date + sender + recipient match would block the item, yet both regests summarise only the clear text (Sweden's English suit, the Öttingen-Schertlin feud, the Inquisition, Lorraine-Guise). Snippet probes for Maximilian, römisch, Kaiser, Wahl, Zettel and Chiffre return 0 in the volume. Further traps: (1) the enciphered event, Ferdinand's approach to the Electors to elect Maximilian King of the Romans, is printed in Goetz 1891 and Kluckhohn I nr. 148 (the Palatine side, 30-31 Dec 1561); (2) the Wiesbaden HHStA 171 M excerpts are of the clear letter; (3) the unseen Dresden minute (Loc. 9941/3 f.268-269, 'met een Zettel') could carry the enclosure in clear and would lower the item to N0 in substance; (4) Regan's 1995 Southampton PhD cites Demandt nr. 115.

item: m0002 letter fragment, ANTT PT/TT/CLNH/0086/11 (Condes de Linhares), pp.2-3
final_class: N3 (key ours)
near_miss: The same printed ANTT catalogue notes 'Esta junta a decifracao' for a different letter in the fonds. Generic decoded phrases ('pela memoria do', 'supprir o seu lugar') return hundreds of unrelated IA and Google Books hits. The sender-family edition (Textos Politicos, Economicos e Financeiros, 1993) and Mansuy-Diniz Silva's 2006 biography are unread (403 or no copy), so a gate requiring 'edition read' would hold it at blocked, not pass it.

item: identification of the key's 'o Diccionario' as Vieyra, A New Pocket Dictionary (London 1809)
final_class: N3 (key ours)
near_miss: The dictionary itself is public on IA (newpocketdiction00viey). The MNE exhibition 'O segredo da escrita' mentions a 1965 'Dicionario da Cifra do MNE' (unrelated, 20th century). The ANTT catalogue's only dictionary mention is a 'Dicionario Geografico do Reino' in an unrelated memorandum. A keyword gate on cifra plus dicionario, or on 'the book is public', would have tripped on these.

item: WVO 5551, Jan van Nassau to William of Orange, Cologne, 17 Apr 1574, the two cipher lines at p3 top (26 of 32 codes, key ours from 4613/4615's period decipherment)
final_class: N3 (V-TX; held by the second audit V-TX2; gate 2 closed by V-GATE2), D2
near_miss: Glawischnig (1973) cites this exact letter in a footnote: '17.4.1574 Köln und 21.4. Wesel, JvN an WvO. KHA A XI 5, auch STAMa 4f Nld. 165'. The citation covers the letter's clear content only (snippet view; the cipher lines were not found printed). WVO's own Inhoud also summarises the clear report. A second copy exists at Marburg (STAMa 4f Nld. 165, unchecked). Two decoys also surfaced: Kervyn, Relations politiques VII no. MMDCCLXXVI (Lumbres to Leicester, Cologne, 17 July 1574), and the Groen IV p.91 footnote on a different unsolved passage. A date+sender+recipient gate would trip on Glawischnig even though the cipher plaintext is not in it.

item: ink 54, Saint-Gouard to Charles IX, Madrid, 7 Sept 1572, BnF fr.16104 f.173r-v
final_class: N3 (VIV54-A1 and VER1-VIV), D1, key published (Tomokiyo)
near_miss: The leaf carries a partial period decipherment: 8 legible interlinear fragments, about 60 letters, against about 1,950 tokens. The key is published (Tomokiyo, henryiii.htm). 'Saint-Gouard' '7 septembre 1572' hits Catherine de Médicis IV's table (her letter to La Mothe-Fénelon). RQH 35 (1884) narrates a courier reaching Madrid on 7 Sept, and Kervyn cites Saint-Gouard letters of 2, 12 and 19 Sept. A 'gloss on leaf' or 'published key' gate would block it, though no plaintext is in print.

item: ink 53, Saint-Gouard to the duc d'Anjou, Madrid, 5 Sept 1572, BnF fr.16104 ff.170r-171v
final_class: N3 (VIV53-A1 and VER1-VIV), D1, key published (Tomokiyo)
near_miss: Its same-date sibling is ink 50 (5 Sept 1572, to the King): Gachard II prints it as entry L and it has a clerk decipherment (ink 51). Two citations also point at ink 50's plain passage: d'Ars (1884) p.43 cites '5 septembre 1572, Ms. Bibl. nat. F. fr. 16104', and Ribera (2007) n.18 cites 'de Madrid, le 5 septembre 1572; BNF, Fr., 16104'. Ribera n.139 paraphrases an undated 1572 Saint-Gouard letter to Anjou, still open, which is why this is not N4. The leaf carries a partial period gloss (6 words, about 45 letters). A date+sender+shelfmark gate that omits the recipient would wrongly mark it solved.

item: ink 63, cipher part of Saint-Gouard to Charles IX, Madrid, 10 Oct 1573, BnF fr.16105 ff.190r-194r
final_class: N3 (VIV63-A1 and VER1-VIV), D1, key published (Tomokiyo)
near_miss: Gachard II LXIII prints a summary of the plain part, flagged '(En partie chiffrée, sans le déchiffrement)'. d'Ars (1884) cites 'Saint-Gouard à Charles IX, 10 octobre 1573, F. fr. 16105' and paraphrases the plain passport passage. Gachard LXVII-LXVIII (20 Oct 1573) prints a deciphered letter on the same topics (the grand commandeur, Flanders), and Morel-Fatio (1904) quotes the 20 Oct dispatch on Requesens. Flament (1996), a monograph on exactly this embassy, is unread. A gate keyed on date+sender+recipient+shelfmark would trip on Gachard and d'Ars, though only the plain part is in print.

item: BnF Espagnol 144 f.22r-v, unsigned instruction to the abbé de Mercy, Barneton 6 June 1648 (488 of 529 at S)
final_class: N4, key ours, D2
near_miss: Lonchay, Cuvelier and Lefèvre, Correspondance de la Cour d'Espagne IV (1933) no.183 p.71 calendars Leopold Wilhelm's June 1648 dispatch with the mission's substance (Elector of Brandenburg, 3,000 infantry); Cuvelier-Lefèvre VI p.647 names the abbé de Mercy and 'tient un chiffre' in June 1648 (a different letter); Morel-Fatio 1892 catalogue lists 'Autre instruction chiffrée pour le même. Barneton, 6 juin 1648'; Bourdeau's 1 Oct 2026 cyphersolver page reproduces and corrects our reading. A gate on recipient+month+'chiffre' or on 'mission content in print' would have blocked a real N4

item: BnF fr.3621 f.130r (no.116), Dinteville to Nevers, Langres 4 July 1592, two cipher passages (527 signs)
final_class: N3, key period, D1
near_miss: Revue de Champagne et de Brie t.XII (1882) p.341 calendars this very letter (same date, place, addressee, footnote 'En chiffres') with a summary and quoted passage, all from the clear text; 1899 reprint; BnF Catalogue des manuscrits français (1868) entry for no.116; sibling f.128 printed in full on p.340. item: BnF Clairambault 1161, six 'Advis de flandres' cipher leaves, c. 1570 (3,389 signs, 67% C/S)
final_class: N3, key ours, D1
near_miss: The title 'Avis de Flandre, chiffrés' is printed in the BnF finding aid and in Lauer's Clairambault catalogue t.II (1923) p.332; the c186R leaf carries its own contemporary marginal gloss (clear French) deciphering one 220-sign block; 'Advis de flandres' is a stock phrase that hits Vertot's Noailles Ambassades and Wesenbeke; the gloss idiom hits Catherine de Médicis's letters. A naive 'title/phrase in print' gate would have fired

item: C. Sign-to-letter table (key.tsv) for Tomokiyo's sign numbers 06-24
final_class: search-level N3 scope only (not a plaintext claim; no prior sign table located)
near_miss: The plaintext of every word the table reads has been in print since 1842 (Surtees) and 1910 (Boyd); the transcription is Tomokiyo's public Cryptiana file; five numeric codes in the same letters were already identified in print (Haynes 1992). A gate on 'plaintext public' would have blocked it, though the narrow artefact itself survives

item: SHStA Dresden Loc. 694/08 f.410 lower block (P.S., Manteuffel to Flemming, Berlin, Nov 1712), 216 code tokens decoded with Krauske's 1893 manuscript table
final_class: N4 (N3 at VERIFY-MANT, raised by AUDIT2-MANT; D2 since DEPTH-MH, 8 Oct 2026)
near_miss: A naive 'is anything public?' gate would have blocked this item on four counts. (1) Acta Borussica, Behördenorganisation I (1894), co-edited by Krauske, who made the key, prints decoded extracts from the same Loc. 694 file, including Nr. 82, a Manteuffel-to-Flemming report of November 1712 (p.285), with his 'Chiffre für Graf Christoph Dhona' notes. Sender, recipient, month and archive file all match. (2) Sibling leaves f.467 and f.468 carry period interlinear decipherments (N0). (3) Droysen IV.1 quotes Manteuffel's 1712 reports, including a Stettin memoir on the same topic. (4) DECODE record 4999 lists a 1717 Flemming-Manteuffel key. Only a full-text search of the volume with controls showed that the f.410 subjects (Queen of England, Swedes, peace, Stettin) occur nowhere in it

item: no.77, BnF fr.3252 f.117r, Birago to Nevers, Saluces 13 Mar 1572 (279 signs; S 224 after D2-B117M)
final_class: N4 (AUDIT 3 raised from N3), key published (Tomokiyo 1572 Nevers-Birago), D1 'fragments read', judge FAIL
near_miss: The key is public (Tomokiyo's printed 1572 table, from fr.3251 no.87's attached decipherment), and sister 1572 letters in fr.3251 were already read with it. The 1874 printed BnF catalogue lists the item ('Lettre, avec chiffre ... 13 mars 1572'). Bourdeau's Gallica sweep has fr.3252 as a candidate row, and Tomokiyo's unsolved.htm calls the fr.3251 group decipherable 'using keys reconstructed from already deciphered materials'. A gate on 'key published' or 'item catalogued in print' would have blocked an unread letter.

item: no.30, BnF fr.3252 f.47r, Birago to Nevers, Saluzzo 26 Apr 1571 (771 signs)
final_class: N3 (class without a reading: S 6 of 771, six isolated o's)
near_miss: In the same volume, no.24 (f.36-37, three weeks earlier) is N0 with a clerk's interlinear decipherment and is flagged 'avec chiffre et déchiffrement' in the 1874 catalogue; no.30 is only 'avec chiffre'. Tomokiyo published the Ceppo-Nevers key from fr.4702 ff.36-37, the same folio numbers as fr.3252 ff.36-37, a coincidence the auditor had to rule out. A same-volume sibling or folio-number match would have blocked it wrongly.

item: WVO 11008, KHA A 11/XI 15, William of Orange ('George Certain') to Louis of Nassau ('Lambert Certain'), Cologne 12 Aug 1572, five numeral runs
final_class: N3 (KHF2-VERIFIER 7 Oct; AUD2-WVO11008 8 Oct kept), key period, D1 after AUDIT 2 lowered D2
near_miss: Many related things are public. The cover names are printed in Kervyn, Huguenots et Gueux II and in 1860s polemics, and Groen's Archives 1re série prints other 'Lambert Certain' letters (52 IA hits). The 1572 Orange-Nassau table is printed (Nepveu tot Ameyde, Konst- en Letterbode). De Leeuw 2000 cites a same-key sibling (Orange to Jan, 21 Sept 1572, Groen III) solved by Van der Kemp in 1836. Alba's 21 Aug 1572 letter in Gachard, Corr. Philippe II vol. II, gives the Duke of Holstein's movements. A naive 'cover name, key or sibling in print' gate would have blocked an unprinted letter; the Waanders 2022 ToC is still unread.

item: Mél. Colbert 127 f.349 cipher passages P2/P3, R. de Gravel to Colbert, Ratisbon 29 Jan 1665
final_class: N3 (two audits), D2 ~73%, key published (Tomokiyo 1672 Colbert-Gravel)
near_miss: Tomokiyo's louisxiv0.htm lists this very letter (f.349, 'not deciphered') and publishes the 1672 key used. DECODE has record R2678 (status Non-decrypted). Bourdeau's catalogue has a row ('Not attacked'). Depping t.III prints other Gravel-to-Colbert letters of 1665, and Haug 2015 studies the same pension system (unread). A gate on 'shelfmark present in Cryptiana/DECODE/Bourdeau' or on sender + recipient + year in Depping would wrongly block it.

item: Baluze 170 f.229r-v bare cipher passage, Chavigny to d'Avaux, Amiens 25 Aug 1640 (366 tokens)
final_class: N3 (two audits), D2 ~29%, key published (Tomokiyo D'Avaux)
near_miss: DECODE R2761 (Baluze 170 f.228-230) carries Status 'Decrypted', but only the key is attached (Inline Plaintext No). That status is mirrored in Bourdeau SOLVED_CATALOGUE.md l.239 and Aymeloglu's decode-catalog.csv. Tomokiyo quotes one fragment of f.228 and publishes the key. Boppe 1887 prints a letter to d'Avaux dated 25 Aug 1640, from his father on other matters. A gate on DECODE status or on recipient + date would block it.

item: f.89 letter (19 Sept 1578), unprinted paragraphs f.89r, f.89v, f.90r, f.90v L01-L09/L27, f.91r (1,525 M + 198 U)
final_class: N3 but D1 (not a unique solve)

item: f.119 letter (15 Oct 1578), unprinted paragraphs f.119r, f.119v upper, f.119v L02-L06, f.120r L05-L08 (660 M + 96 U)
final_class: N3 but D1 (not a unique solve)

item: A. BnF fr.4712 f.10r, Nevers to the duchesse de Nevers (BnF 1895: 'i octobre 1592'): six of 37 cipher numbers carried from f.13r's glosses (82 82 'D. n.', 21 21 'Berry', 12 12 'b. Pal.'), grade C conditional on one same-writer judgement
final_class: N3 (one audit; D1, 16% C, 'fragments read'; key period)
near_miss: A naive 'is anything public about this shelfmark or cipher?' gate would trip several times, though nothing deciphers f.10: Tomokiyo's nevers.htm lists f.10 (as 'undeciphered') and partly reads f.13 ('25 appears to read Paris'); the BnF 1895 catalogue entry describes and dates the cipher passage ('a une partie chiffrée'); the same volume's f.13r carries a period interlinear decipherment, the source of every value carried; and Boltanski 2006 and Hamilton 2024 cite fr.4712 (f°7, f°100). Not yet N4: Boltanski was not read in full.
